hook_text: Wash 58 cars a month and you lose money. Wash 60 and you make money. Here is how to find that line.
clip_script: Shine on Wheels needs R13 500 to start: pressure washer, tanks, vacuum, branding, permit. R6 000 from savings, R7 500 from family. Every wash earns R120 but uses R30 of soap, water and petrol, so each wash leaves R90. Every month there are R5 300 of fixed costs: the helper's wage, rent, phone, insurance, whether you wash one car or a hundred. So how many washes pay the fixed costs? 5 300 divided by 90. 58.9. Round up: 59. That is the break-even point. Below 59, a loss. Above it, a profit. The goal is 120 washes: R14 400 in, R3 600 out on products, R5 300 fixed. Profit R5 500. That is a business plan a bank can believe.
visual_style: Equipment icons stacking into an R13 500 total, coins dropping R90 at a time into a jar until it reaches the R5 300 line at wash 59.
pacing: Fast setup of costs, a slow count to the break-even line, quick payoff to R5 500.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the break-even point for your own business idea.
